result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by high-rise residential buildings and signalized intersections. While sidewalks and pedestrian signals are present, the lack of visible crosswalk markings and sightline obstructions from parked cars create significant safety gaps.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right side of the roadway in the foreground.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalk
hazards.description: Despite the presence of pedestrian signals, there are no visible painted crosswalks on the pavement to guide pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface near the signalized poles.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define the pedestrian path and increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection with a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and parked vehicles near the crossing create visibility and exposure risks for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars on the right side of the street are positioned close to the crosswalk, potentially blocking sight lines between drivers and pedestrians entering the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection, adjacent to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic without a central refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, across the main roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility (daylighting).

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and sidewalks, but the wide roadway creates a significant crossing distance for pedestrians. The environment lacks traffic calming measures or pedestrian refuge islands, which increases exposure to vehicle traffic in a mixed-use area.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the intersection increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic without a refuge.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Calming
hazards.description: The wide, open asphalt design and lack of vertical elements like trees or curb extensions may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a median or refuge island in the center of the wide crossing to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Plant trees along the sidewalk to provide a physical buffer and create a 'visual narrowing' effect to slow traffic.

result.summary: The intersection features a high-visibility zebra crosswalk and traffic signals, but the crossing distance is significant across multiple lanes and buffers. While sidewalks and a bike lane are present, the lack of physical pedestrian refuges or curb extensions increases exposure to traffic.
